ideas.pitch: A hyper-local coordination PWA that matches restaurant and bakery surplus food with nearby volunteers and low-income households for safe, timed distribution.
ideas.problem_statement: Restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets and households regularly have surplus food, while people nearby may struggle to afford meals. The challenge is often coordination, timing and safe distribution.
ideas.title: SurplusSync
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly tackles the published online round problem statement with a functioning PWA, matching the proven pattern of clear measurable social impact and a live working demo.

ideas.pitch: A spatial mapping web app that logs unrecorded informal waste pickers' routes and informal sorting hubs to quantify city-level recycling that never hits official databases.
ideas.problem_statement: The Invisible City: Waste nobody counts and people who keep everything working but never appear in any database.
ideas.title: GhostAudit
ideas.why_it_could_win: Aligns tightly with the core theme of 'The Invisible City' by bringing invisible workers and uncounted waste into a visible dashboard, highly appealing to jury members looking for original thinking.

ideas.pitch: An audio-first collection portal that records, translates, and clusters vernacular voice complaints from street vendors and sanitation staff into structured municipal tickets.
ideas.problem_statement: The Invisible City: Voices no system understands and needs nobody says out loud.
ideas.title: VoiceLane
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages audio processing and simple UI to solve a painfully real city communication gap, winning on problem sharpness and sound execution within a 7-hour build window.

ideas.pitch: An offline-first peer support and emergency alert network designed specifically for gig workers and night-shift urban service providers operating in blind spots.
ideas.problem_statement: The Invisible City: People who keep everything working but never appear in any database.
ideas.title: ShiftLink
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on human empathy and real-world utility for marginalized urban workers, directly hitting the jury's criteria of explaining why the idea matters to a real user.

ideas.pitch: A crowdsourced hazard logger built for informal settlements to map localized waterlogging and blocked drainage channels that municipal maps miss.
ideas.problem_statement: The Invisible City: Finding something real that the city overlooks, and building technology that makes it heard, seen, counted or said.
ideas.title: DrainWatch
ideas.why_it_could_win: Features an immediately testable photo-upload and map-pinning flow that lets judges test the live demo right from their phones during the pitch.
